location.mountain: Dong Ding (part of Fengshan mountain range)

description.short: Classic Taiwanese oolong from Dong Ding Mountain — balanced, nutty, with gentle roasting
description.overview: One of the most famous and historically defining Taiwanese oolongs, establishing the benchmark of what the world knows as 'Taiwanese oolong'.
description.leaf: Tightly rolled dark green spheres with a brownish roasted hue
description.aroma: Nutty, subtly floral, with warm roasted overtones
description.taste: Harmonious, nutty, gentle natural sweetness with a savory toasted note
description.aftertaste: Moderately long, clean, roasted nutty finish
description.processing: Plucking → withering → tossing/shaking → kill-green → tight ball rolling → baking/roasting (ranging from light to medium-heavy according to producer tradition)

history.origin: According to legend, the cultivar was brought to Taiwan from mainland China (Anxi, Fujian) by local scholar Lin Fengchi in the 19th century, returning with saplings after passing the imperial civil service exams.
history.development: Dong Ding mountain, with its misty climate and moderate altitude, proved ideal for oolong bushes, quickly becoming the model terroir for Taiwanese tea culture.
history.modern: The name 'Dong Ding' became so renowned that it is often used (sometimes loosely) to describe the roasted Taiwanese oolong style broadly, even when crafted in neighboring townships.
interestingFacts: The mountain's name translates literally to 'Frozen Peak' — folklore tells of slippery trails where tea pluckers had to grip the hillside with their toes to ascend.
Dong Ding is one of the few Taiwanese oolongs that traditionally feature substantial charcoal or oven baking, contrasting with modern unroasted high-mountain oolongs.
